answers.answer: They cannot first win at the next Wake: at that Wake, they are checked for Usurper victory before the title flips from Oathkeeper to Usurper. They can first win at the following Wake, if they still hold the title and meet the goal. If the title is lost, the Usurper win is prevented; taking it again resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence. They can also win at the end of round 8 if they are still Usurper then.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake”; losing title prevents the win.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win also requires an Exile to have their true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, “most” must mean strictly more than every other player; a tie does not count.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; Visionary victory: “at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined” and “strictly more than every other player.”

answers.answer: At the end of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll only if the Oathkeeper is the Chancellor or a Citizen. The game ends on a 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. If an Exile is Oathkeeper/Usurper, the roll is prevented.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: “at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7” and results “6 / 5–6 / 3–6”; an Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

answers.answer: At the end of round 8, check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins; Chancellor wins unless a qualifying Citizen Successor wins alone instead. (2) Otherwise an Exile Usurper wins. (3) Otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins; if several qualify, priority is Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith. (4) Otherwise Empire wins, with the Chancellor winning unless a qualifying Citizen Successor wins alone. Thus an Exile Oathkeeper alone does not prevent the final Empire fallback.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion numbered priority, including “even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.”

answers.answer: Supremacy: Citizen holds more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: holds Darkest Secret. Protection: holds People's Favor. Devotion: holds Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a revealed true Vision or by becoming Usurper; Citizens and Chancellor cannot win by either route.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table gives each Citizen Successor goal; Visionary victory says “Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.”

answers.answer: During Wake, if you hold People's Favor, choose to put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Do not remove its last favor: if it has 1, add one if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If the banner is already Mob-side, repeat this choice once. After the choice(s), check whether it has 6 or more favor and flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at this final check does not cause an extra payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake, step 1: “Never remove its last favor”; “if banner is already Mob-side, repeat”; “Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob.”

answers.answer: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; save unspent Supply; then optionally use Rest powers once each in chosen order. Chancellor/Exile refresh according to their remaining personal-bank warbands (Chancellor: 18+ = 6, 11–17 = 5, 4–10 = 4, 0–3 = 3; Exile: 9+ = 6, 4–8 = 5, 0–3 = 4). Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including the leftmost, not by counting purple warbands. Save remaining Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at the leftmost space (7 Supply).
answers.evidence: Rest: mandatory order, steps 1–5; Citizen “exact Chancellor marker space”; save remaining Supply “one extra space left per unspent Supply.”

answers.answer: Search uses either the world deck or the discard pile for the region containing your pawn, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. A world-deck Search costs 2 Supply at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, or 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that world-deck cost with 2, while other applicable modifiers still apply. Draw 3 (or fewer if the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it); you cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck draw one at a time; upon drawing a Vision announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile neither stops drawing nor advances the track. If the source empties, draw only the remaining cards; no reshuffle is implied.
answers.evidence: Search: “Choose either world deck or your pawn's region discard pile”; the cost schedule; “Drawing Visions from a discard does not stop drawing or advance the track.”

answers.answer: Discarded cards go facedown onto the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, with multiple discards ordered as chosen; never use the same-region pile. Cards from hand or advisers use the pile after the region of the discarder’s pawn. When discarding a card at a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card’s region instead of the pawn’s region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching suit bank; secrets on it go to the acting player’s board facedown.
answers.evidence: Discard destinations: “When discarding a card at a site in another region, apply that cycle to the card’s region”; favor and secrets disposition stated there.

answers.answer: The adviser limit is up to 3 total cards, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser (respecting locked cards); if the incoming card changes the limit, use the new limit before playing it, and use the lowest limit if there are multiple limit-changing cards. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power; later it can be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action, and it may be peeked at. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when another rule permits or requires it. An Exile may reveal a true Vision faceup in the separate Revealed Vision space, which does not use an adviser slot; doing so replaces and discards the Exile’s previous revealed Vision. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search—Adviser and True Vision options; Minor actions: “play or discard a facedown adviser”; Scoring section: revealed Vision rules.

answers.answer: Both actions cost 1 Supply and use an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn’s site; it must have no favor or secrets. Muster puts 1 favor on it, then moves 2 warbands from your personal bank to your board (a Citizen gains purple warbands); Relics and ruins are ineligible, and ruling the site is unnecessary. Trade chooses either: put 1 secret on the card to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card’s suit bank; or put 2 favor on the card to gain 1 secret per matching faceup adviser from the shared bank. Facedown advisers do not match. With no matching advisers, the second Trade option gains zero secrets, but its 2-favor cost is still paid. Gains are limited by available favor/warbands; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections: eligible empty card and pawn site; costs and gains; “With no matching advisers gain zero secrets.”

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. A banner may be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently holds and place the paid favor on it; distribute its old favor one at a time to suit banks, starting at a chosen bank and proceeding away from the world deck through the bank order and wrapping as needed. Do not return old favor to its previous holder. Flip it to normal side if Mob. There is no seizure penalty for Recovering. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds; place the paid secrets on it, the new holder takes 1 old secret, and the previous holder takes the rest (if recovering from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from the shared bank, the remainder stays there).
answers.evidence: Recover section: relic costs and People's Favor/Darkest Secret recovery procedures.

answers.answer: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, their pawn’s site must contain at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that holder’s faceup advisers. One such mismatching card suffices even if other cards match. If the holder has no faceup advisers, a suited card at the site is recoverable because it matches none; an empty site or a ruin-only site also permits recovery. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. Recovery from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.
answers.evidence: Darkest Secret protection: “at least one suited card at their pawn’s site whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers”; empty and ruin-only sites protect it.

answers.answer: Choose as defender any other player who rules your pawn’s site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. Normally at least one target must be at your pawn’s site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of the defender’s sites anywhere on the map, one defense die per site. If the defender’s pawn is at your site, you may additionally target any of their relics there (using the relic’s printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to resources on the banner), or their pawn and board favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender’s relic target can itself satisfy the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2: defender eligibility and targets, including “any of defender’s sites anywhere on map” and co-located relic exception.

answers.answer: The attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force. Defense dice come from targets/modifiers; the Oathkeeper adds 1 defense die and the Usurper 2. In the roll, count shields and double them for each double-symbol (multipliers stack); then add all defending warbands at targeted sites and the defender’s board force if their pawn is at the attacker’s site or a targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only. Each skull on the attack roll immediately kills one of the attacker’s own force warbands. Count full swords, then add one attack for each pair of hollow swords; an unpaired hollow sword is zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving own force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing, must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never excess. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower is a defender win.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4–5: attack dice limit, defense additions, skulls, hollow swords and strict-win/sacrifice rules.

answers.answer: On attacker victory, first the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, and returns the rest to its board; resolve defeated-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number of surviving force warbands, including zero, on any targeted sites. With zero placed, a site is left to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners; when a banner is seized other than by Recover, burn 2 of its resources down to a minimum of 1, and People's Favor flips to Mob. If the defender’s pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may independently burn half the defender’s board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; if Shrouded Wood’s enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go, that overrides the attacker’s destination choice. Then resolve the attacker’s victorious plan effects, and discard plans saying “At end, discard.”
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8: defeat precedes targets; step 7 covers zero garrisons, seized banners and forced travel/banishment.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender’s permission if their pawn is at the attacker’s site or a targeted site. Defender/Allies share Campaign modifiers and powers as one defending side, including the Oathkeeper defense bonus; allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker’s site or a targeted site. They may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, but not other players’ advisers; a shared plan is usable once total by one user, who pays its cost. The declared defender decides order, timing, priority, and disagreements among Allies. Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor’s board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens’ boards stay there. If a Citizen attacks Chancellor or another Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for the Campaign; if Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make every Citizen non-Imperial; only the specified player loses Imperial status temporarily.
answers.evidence: Imperial defense bullets; Campaign step 1 specifies the temporary non-Imperial cases.

answers.answer: Base Travel Supply costs (from region to region) are: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, any region 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not only an adjacent slot. If the destination is facedown, reveal it and place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and its printed number of facedown relics from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Free Travel is the final override: an applicable power saying spend no Supply makes cost zero despite an increase. Relevant site examples: Coast-to-Coast costs 1 and ignores Narrow Pass; from Charming Valley add 1; from Shrouded Wood costs 2 and ignores Narrow Pass and Hidden Place; Buried Giant may let you flip a board secret facedown for no Supply and to ignore Narrow Pass. Entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by a rule/power. The summary does not give a general numerical list of every possible fixed-cost or free-Travel card power.
answers.evidence: Travel table and cost order; site-power bullets for Coasts, Charming Valley, Shrouded Wood, Buried Giant.

answers.answer: The current Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot use the Scepter or make an offer on the turn they took it. The offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the recipient flips to Citizen and replaces all their board/map warbands with purple (if purple is short, they choose which to remove and replace), discards any revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if accepting during their turn, refreshes to full leftmost Supply, and exchanges the promised pieces. Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. The offer cannot promise more or less than exactly one Reliquary relic as its required gift; other agreed exchanges are additional.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play: Grand Scepter, Offer, and Acceptance sections.

answers.answer: For the next Oath, a winner who won by Vision alone must use the Oath matching that Vision; a winner who won by another method or multiple methods chooses any Oath except the current one, and saves the goal in the World Box. Chronicle Citizenship is a free separate permission: an Exile winner flips all Citizen boards, including boxed boards, to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile flips their board to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle all denizens remaining in play (excluding those retained at sites, Archive, or Dispossessed), then make a 12-card top stack from 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions and an 18-card next stack from 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions; remaining denizens go below. It is not 14 cards because the Chronicle aid’s “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; the correct top stack is 10 denizens + 2 Visions = 12.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle steps 1–2 and 9: Oath choice, free Chronicle Citizenship, and corrected “10 denizens plus 2 random Visions = 12.”
